Earlier in March, Apple announced the discontinuation of the Mac Pro, and confirmed that it has no plans to release new Mac Pro hardware.

A new report from Bloomberg today further reveals the behind-the-scenes story of Apple's Mac Pro strategy, including a surprising detail...

The inside story of Apple shelving the Mac Pro plans

In the latest edition of the "Power On" newsletter, Mark Gurman points out that Apple internally "had no plans to give up on the Mac Pro from the start." Gurman once again mentions a claim reported earlier: Apple's original idea was to launch a chip called "Extreme" on top of the "Ultra" chip.

The report quoted: "Apple was developing two chips, namely M2 Extreme and M3 Extreme, but eventually terminated the project based on cost and demand considerations."

As for the specific Mac Pro hardware that was already developed, Gurman said Apple had two models (internal codenames J170 and J190) under development at the time, but ultimately neither was released to the market.

The most intriguing detail in the report is that one of the models used an Intel processor:

Apple finally discontinued the Mac Pro in March, removing it from its official website, and guiding buyers to purchase the Mac Studio instead. Although the discontinuation was foreshadowed, for Mac Pro enthusiasts, it still marks the quiet end of an era.

Apple has abandoned the Mac Pro product line, and has chosen not to launch the "Extreme" chip in the Apple Silicon era. What do you think of this decision? Feel free to share your opinions in the comment section.
